category_title: Noncompliant students who misbehave due to boredom or environmental distractions
minimal_context: Melinda is participating in a 45-minute Power Play test-preparation activity in a classroom where other students are present.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright everyone, it is time for our 45-minute Power Play test-preparation activity. Please open your materials and begin working.

STUDENT: (Laughs loudly with a peer) Sometimes we talk in class and I can't concentrate. If I hear students talking I start talking too.

TUTOR: Melinda, please lower your voice and get back to your assignment.

STUDENT: There is a lot of talking in here. When my friends talk to me, I don't want to be rude, so I talk back to them. It is easier for me to concentrate in other classes.

TUTOR: You just need to focus on the test prep right now.

STUDENT: (Stands up and slams the classroom door) I get mad during Power Play! I was bored. I'm going to the bathroom, I talk a lot when I go there anyway.

options.A: Provide Melinda with warnings of upcoming transitions before moving to different parts of the test-preparation activity.
options.B: Ask Melinda more frequently if she understands everything about the current test-preparation assignment during the activity.
options.C: Focus on Melinda's positive behaviors, paying attention to and verbalizing her positive actions during the activity.
options.D: Allow Melinda to keep her materials on the condition that she does not show them to her friends, and break off for a restroom break.
